source.title: Comparative Analysis of Activation Functions in Recurrent Neural Network: An Application to Indonesian Inflation Forecasting
source.authors: Rahmadi Yotenka; Muhammad Muhajir; Hermansah; P. Rodrigues

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: It compares SGD with AdaGrad on Indonesian inflation forecasting, a new time-series setting for the adaptive-optimizer performance question.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own optimizer, activation-function, learning-rate, epoch, and forecasting-model comparisons. The optimizer comparison bears on V4; the activation, learning-rate, epoch, and forecasting-model results do not directly test a listed version.
record.test_reason: Table 1 compares held-out performance of an adaptive optimizer, AdaGrad, with SGD under the same stated learning rate and epoch budget. This extends V4's optimizer question to inflation forecasting, outside its image and language benchmarks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct: the authors favor SGD over AdaGrad and select Logistic-SGD as their best configuration, reporting 93.41% training accuracy, 93.57% testing accuracy, and final forecast SMAPE 0.14812. They report that it outperforms ETS, ARIMA, FFNN, and GRNN. However, Logistic does not beat Gompertz on SMAPE in Table 2, and the selected configuration's Table 4 test SMAPE is 0.16371, distinct from the final comparison value.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares SGD with AdaGrad, not Adam or the optimizer comparisons in V4; it forecasts Indonesian inflation using a standard RNN and reports training and testing accuracy and SMAPE.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer, activation function, learning rate, and epoch count changed reported results.

fits_no_version.finding: Logistic and Gompertz activations outperform Tanh; Logistic has higher reported accuracy, whereas Gompertz has lower SMAPE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice affects RNN inflation-forecasting performance.

record.peer_reviewed: Mathematical Modelling of Engineering Problems, Vol. 12, No. 3, March 2025
record.problems: The optimizer comparison uses a single dataset and split, and the paper does not report uncertainty estimates. It does not establish whether the optimizer difference persists under broader tuning. Training accuracy and test accuracy are reported, but the V4 question of worse held-out performance despite equal or better training performance is not demonstrated for AdaGrad.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for individual learning rates in Table 3 and epoch values in Table 4 are omitted; these are not direct tests of a listed version, and including all training/test SMAPE and accuracy entries would exceed 60 rows. Table 5 compares forecasting models, but those comparisons do not test a listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in matched architectures and recipes.
Width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

Image and language benchmarks; optimizer-specific learning-rate and decay-schedule tuning; adaptive methods with equal or better training performance; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and word-level language models. Only AdaGrad versus SGD at a shared learning rate and epoch budget is compared.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and its interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the proposed training-split limits_scope verdict: V4 says adaptive methods sometimes lose despite better training performance, not that they must do so. Worse AdaGrad training performance leaves that clause untested. The optimizer comparison uses one split with only 12 test months, no reported uncertainty, and no matched optimizer-specific tuning. Later learning-rate and epoch selection uses test performance, and nominally matching SGD settings have inconsistent values across tables. Table 5's Adam-trained FFNN differs architecturally from the SGD RNN and cannot isolate an optimizer effect.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Network width relative to the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Image-classification and language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large-batch training.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.condition: Standard RNN inflation forecasting with Gompertz activation, shared learning rate 0.05, and 500 epochs.
relationships.reason: R2 and R6 report test SMAPE of 0.15071 for SGD versus 0.80961 for AdaGrad; R4 and R8 also favor SGD on reported accuracy. This supports the optimizer ordering in this new setting.
relationships.display_finding: Reported testing error was lower and reported accuracy higher for SGD than AdaGrad, but the comparison remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: RNN inflation forecasting with Gompertz activation, learning rate 0.05, and 500 epochs
reader_labels.reason: AdaGrad has higher test SMAPE and lower test accuracy than SGD in this setting (R2, R4, R6, R8). The comparison is in a time-series forecasting task, not the image or language benchmarks named in the version.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: AdaGrad also has worse training SMAPE and accuracy, so this result does not show an adaptive method losing held-out performance despite equal or better training performance (R1, R3, R5, R7).
